rites.name: Siathis
rites.text: Siathis is the concept of resonance held by Lyanae during the Singing, the undated sounding in which the first roots of the world condense out of pure tone. It is less a being than a principle that gathers scattered vibration into lasting form.

rites.name: Taurallium
rites.text: Taurallium is a concept of the Lyanae omniverse, a resonant pattern that the first roots are said to have hummed into being during the Singing. In the Age of the first sovereign, it is remembered as the tone that let groves hold their shape while kingdoms grew around them.

rites.name: Kelornen
rites.text: Kelornen is the concept of the first sounding that condensed the roots of Lyanae, a note held before time had a clock. It is remembered in the groves as the pulse that taught growing things how to reach for light.

rites.name: Thornerdeld
rites.text: Thornerdeld is the concept of a thorned root-tone that rang through the Singing, when the first roots of Lyanae gathered out of silence. Ki-bearers of the Holy Age taught that it was the first note that kept the world from unraveling, and temples still hum its pitch.

rites.name: Lyinniel
rites.text: Lyinniel is the concept of the Singing, the undated sounding by which the first roots of Lyanae condense out of silence. In the Holy Age of flame, temples and orders, scholars speak of it as the tone that gave matter its first grip on itself.

rites.name: Osutalarira
rites.text: Osutalarira is the concept of the first sounding that gathers the roots of Lyanae into shape, a resonance remembered by the temples of the Holy Age as the moment flame first learned to hold its form. It is less a being than a pattern the orders of that age sought to echo in ritual fire and stone.

rites.name: Croste
rites.text: Croste is the concept of a root-sound that condenses as the first foundations of Lyanae take hold during the Singing, a tone that binds drifting matter into lasting ground. In the Age of Sundering it became the measure by which broken bonds were judged, its resonance felt as the grinding of landfall.

rites.name: Lialenanum
rites.text: A soldier sings this early-morning chant to rouse comrades from sleep before dawn. It serves the same stirring purpose as other wake-up songs of the realm.

rites.name: Ameones Toniarnum
rites.text: A blade discipline practiced by a warrior of the old courts. A wandering swordsman later learns it and folds it into his own dueling craft.

rites.name: Ameosiaror
rites.text: A rousing chant performed together by five companions, sung as a call to action before setting out. It binds the voices of the group into one shared cheer.

rites.name: Vales
rites.text: A lilting chant sung by a small horned physician for an island collection, sung to rouse the spirit of a snowy isle of drums.

rites.name: Lyalae
rites.text: Lyalae is the concept of threshold-keeping in Lyanae, the thing that a door remembers about being a door. In the Courts of the second era, Lyalae was invoked by councils that judged whether a passage between worlds should stand or close.

rites.name: Tiranaruta
rites.text: Tiranaruta is a concept in Lyanae, a stillness that the Courts of the first sovereign set down as a law of trial and passage. It is said to hold the threshold between groves and the doors that were raised between worlds.

rites.name: Eliluanwen
rites.text: Eliluanwen is a concept of Lyanae, the stillness a court holds before a verdict is read, personified as a presence that weighs oaths against the shape of the world. In the Age of Sundering it was asked to stand as witness when the old bonds between worlds gave way, and its judgment became the first lintel of the new doors.

rites.name: Coraustes
rites.text: A duelist's discipline in which one wields eight blades at once, gripped by hands and grasping limbs alike. The practitioner coats each edge with a paralyzing venom, and an overdose of a strength-enhancing draught lets the blades cut through metal.

rites.name: Coreollanum
rites.text: A grappling discipline practiced by a sea-dwelling people, whose throws can shape the surrounding water as though it were solid matter. Its masters hold a great edge when fighting beneath the waves.

rites.name: Coriarum
rites.text: A fighting discipline built around strikes delivered with the legs. It was first displayed by a fighter during a great contest held in an open arena.

rites.name: Selliantor
rites.text: A blade discipline that a single named practitioner devised and still applies in combat. It is a method of wielding a sword in several coordinated strikes.

rites.name: Tiaserum
rites.text: A mournful chant composed by a wandering bard, sung to calm the heart before a grim end. The bard later passes it on to a young royal, who learns it while leading a traveling caravan.

rites.name: Seoresia
rites.text: A fighting style practiced by the stout miners of a mountain realm, shaped by the hardy physique of their people. It draws on the unique traits of their kind, much like the water-dwelling warriors' techniques do.

rites.name: Amiantolum
rites.text: A rare inner sense lets a few gifted folk perceive messages carried without speech, drawn from stones, beasts, or the quiet thoughts of others. Most people never learn to hear it at all.

rites.name: Nuarlae
rites.text: Nuarlae is the quiet hour in Lyanae when the makers sow the Weave across the young groves, and the slumbering powers of the land drift into rest. Its sheer act of planting is gentle, yet it threads the whole realm of Ki into one lasting pattern.

rites.name: Tensanira
rites.text: Tensanira is the concept of the Weave, the living lattice the makers plant during the Seeding to hold quiet powers asleep across Lyanae. In the Age of the first sovereign it is understood as the patient thread binding groves to growing kingdoms, a force that gathers slowly rather than strikes.

rites.name: Osunalvaoma
rites.text: Osunalvaoma is the concept of the Weave as it is seeded into Lyanae, the quiet thread that lets the makers' powers lie dormant until a temple wakes them. In the Holy Age of flame and orders, it is the principle by which priests bind fire to their vows and keep the old powers from waking too soon.

rites.name: Thiathora
rites.text: Thiathora is the concept of the Seeding in Lyanae, the moment the makers sink the Weave into the world and the quiet powers fall asleep beneath it. In the Holy Age that follows, temples and orders name this sleep as the proper order of things, and its teachings are kept in flame.

rites.name: Vereornia
rites.text: A chanted verse that tells of a horned healer's heroic alter-ego. It is sung to stir courage and to celebrate a champion who fights in disguise.

rites.name: Leostianum
rites.text: A fighting discipline practiced by a closed lineage of warriors. Its practitioners learn to unleash forceful pulses of concussive energy through strikes.

rites.name: Miallor
rites.text: A striking-based combat discipline taught among skilled sea-folk, shared with a few land-dwellers as well. Its deadliest forms are built for fighting beneath the waves, where its practitioners move with greater force and swiftness.

rites.name: Orirnus
rites.text: A small hymn of glowing notes that a tiny, sturdy wanderer hums to itself. Its melody is sung by that little creature alone.

rites.name: Coraullium Oreontiania
rites.text: A mournful chant sung by a ghostly captain as he sails across the sea on a spectral ship. It accompanies his endless voyage.

rites.name: Ceosanum
rites.text: A lone marksman outwits stronger foes using a crowd of contrived gadgets, trick shots, and clever deceit rather than brute force. Each tool hides a counter for a particular enemy.

rites.name: Elilamae
rites.text: Elilamae is the concept of the Fall in Lyanae, the moment a world's bonds gave way and its pieces scattered into the dark. She is remembered in the Age of Sundering as the reason old oaths were broken and the Pact was sworn among the surviving Shards.

rites.name: Resum
rites.text: A wielder shapes the storms and winds around them using a rod-like staff, guided by deep study of sea currents and atmospheric patterns. Its practitioners can unleash devastating tempests on their foes.

rites.name: Serontum
rites.text: A painted snare binds the mind of a foe through shifting hues. A practitioner of this craft uses colored pigment to lure an opponent into a trance.

rites.name: Caurnus Cillus
rites.text: Two bonded kin glow in matching shades, drawing together when their hues differ and pushing apart when they match. They use this pull and push to move swiftly or gain an edge in combat, a gift that flows from their deep familial bond rather than any cursed relic.

rites.name: Restaria
rites.text: A binding pact sealed between a ruler and his closest servants, granting them strange powers in exchange for total obedience. The bound can be commanded by the ruler's voice from any distance.

rites.name: Vauntium
rites.text: A fighting craft built on tumbling leaps, performance gear, and underhanded tactics. Its practitioners win bouts by mixing spectacle with trickery rather than brute strength.

rites.name: Vellastium
rites.text: A rare and mighty gift that lets its bearer turn their flesh into a natural force and command great quantities of that force. Its name arose after someone heard of another's wielding of such a gift.

rites.name: Rastores
rites.text: A chorus of seven companions raises a shared melody together. It is sung in unison as a song of their band.

rites.name: Ceollases
rites.text: A disciplined craft that lets its practitioner command every limb and internal process of the body with total precision. Those who master it are said to be able to govern even the functions most people never consciously direct.

rites.name: Mernia
rites.text: A hidden inner force that lets beings draw on their own willpower for extraordinary feats. Most creatures never learn to wield it, though it can sense movements, shield the body, or overpower the minds of others.

rites.name: Seresium
rites.text: A spoken-rhythm chant performed by a sea-roaming bard, sung in the voice of a bold captain. It serves as a personal theme tied to that captain's character.

rites.name: Sarosor
rites.text: A chant that the undead sing while they move in unison before an attack. Its performance is a rhythmic dance under a turning mirror ball.

rites.name: Niastaulles
rites.text: A bound power that, once called forth, lets a traveler step between distant places in an instant. It is passed down through sworn pacts granted by a single sovereign to a chosen circle of guardians.

rites.name: Coriases
rites.text: A measure used by a secret enforcement band to read how strong a person is in body. From that reading, a practitioner can judge how far their inner abilities reach.

rites.name: Orastanum
rites.text: A contagion that compels its carriers to press their lips onto others without any will to resist. It was engineered by a scholar and deployed by raiders during an assault on a coastal city.

rites.name: Ryinniel
rites.text: Ryinniel is a tide-drawn sorcerer of the Ki realm's fourth age, whose breath can be bottled into a ripple of pressure that cracks cliffs. He wears the old salt-glass lens of his order to keep the storm from spilling out of his lungs.

rites.name: Nuameilys
rites.text: Nuameilys is a sea-glass spirit of the Ki realm who can sink or lift her own mass at will, turning her body into anything from a feather to a drifting moon-stone. Her gentle weightlessness has kept lighthouse keepers and drowned sailors company for six ages of the Lyanae tides.

rites.name: Veneilwen
rites.text: Veneilwen is a concept of Ki, an ancient tide-spirit sealed in the clouds above the drowned plains of Lyanae during the sixth age. She drifts across the valleys as a pursuing hunter of a restless wanderer, sometimes lending her vapor-born strength to unlikely allies against a shared foe.

rites.name: Elalora
rites.text: Elalora is a sacred concept within the Ki realm of Lyanae, a discipline in which a practitioner fractures their own form into a shimmering constellation of luminous orbs that drift apart and reform at will. Its adherents are said to scatter their presence across the sky of a continent and then gather back into a single flame.

rites.name: Miellys
rites.text: Miellys is a sacred weaver of the Ki realm who drinks from a hushed spring of folded air, letting her slip between neighboring points of space as easily as a thread through a needle. Her temple-bound rites mend tears in the sky and carry the chant of the Lyanae shrines from one world-spire to the next.

rites.name: Ryareth
rites.text: Ryareth is a sky-pilgrim of the Ki realm in the Lyanae omniverse, whose body has fused with a bell-shaped gourd of lightning-wine that lets him glide over any surface without friction. Ryareth's own priesthood hails him as a living tether between storm and stillness, able to hold a falling city-scale mass suspended in the air for a single breath.

rites.name: Mianneth
rites.text: Mianneth is a verdant warden of the Ki realm's sixth era, a cloistered keeper who learned to bloom whole groves into being at a word. Her gift lets her call forests up from bare stone in an instant, binding roots to the ruins of older wars.

rites.name: Elaenwen
rites.text: Elaenwen is a concept of the Ki realm in the Lyanae omniverse, a resonance of tidal will that exists only within the second age's drowned choirs. It is said to be the quiet pressure that lets a single voice steer vast currents and the great tide-beasts that answer to them.
